chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, who said:
The deceased is washed with three washings: once with sidr, once with water into which camphor is put, and another time with pure water; then he is shrouded.
And he عليه السلام said: My father wrote in his وصيّة: that I should shroud him in three garments, one of them being a mantle of hibarah, another cloth, and a shirt.

I said: And why did he write this? He said: For fear of what people would say. And after that we bound him with a turban, and we split the earth for him because he was heavy-bodied, and he instructed me to raise the grave above the ground by four outspread fingers, and he mentioned that sprinkling the grave with water is good.

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lote leaves used in one of the washings of the deceased
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave to be raised and sprinkled with water
key_terms.الْكَافُورُ: camphor placed in the water for one of the washings
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْقَرَاحِ: plain pure water used for the final washing
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person whose funeral rites are being described
key_terms.غَسَلَاتٍ: the ritual washings performed for the dead body
key_terms.وَصِيَّتِهِ: his testamentary instruction concerning burial arrangements

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed, shrouded, and buried according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out rulings and practices concerning the preparation of the deceased, including the three ritual washings, shrouding, and aspects of burial. It also preserves the وصيّة of the Imam’s father regarding his shroud and grave, showing both legal guidance and established funerary sunnah in Shia tradition.
